full_judgment:
This Rule at the instances of the defendant-petitioner is directed against the judgment and decree dated 4.3.80 and 10.3.80 respectively of the Subordinate Judge Kushtia passed in Title Appeal No. 40 of 1977 affirming the judgment and decree dated 30.4.77 and 9.5.77 respectively passed by the Munsif, 1st. Court Kushtia in Title Suit No. 339 of 1970 decreeing the suit on contest. 

 4. The plaintiff examined "4 witnesses and the defendant examined himself only. Plaintiff No. 1 as PW 1 deposed that he sold the suit land on behalf of the minor son and that there was an oral agreement to the effect that the Iand would be reconveyed within 7 years on repayment of the consideration money. He further deposed that a salish took place in their local Union Parishad on the basis of an application filed by the plaintiff over the suit land and in the salish it was decided that the defendant would reconvey the suit land if the plaintiff pays Tk. 1000.00 to the defendant within the month of Aswin but the defendant did not reconvey the suit land as per the term of the salish. PW 4 Abdul Jalil Shaikh, Chairman of the Local Union Parishad deposed that a salish was held over the suit land between the parties and it was decided in the salish that the plaintiff would pay Tk. 1000.00 to the defendant within the month of Aswin of the year. Of salish and on receipt of the said amount the defendant would reconvey the suit land. Thus it appears that the plaintiff has based his claim for getting the land reconveyed according to the oral agreement as well as on the settlement arrived at in the salish. Defendant-petitioner who examined himself as DW 1 deposed that he has been possessing the suit land since his. purchase and plaintiff dispossessed him during the liberation war and after dispossession he filed an application to the local Union Parishad against the plaintiff and there was settlement in respect of the disputed land by the chairman. The sale deed executed and registered on 2.10.63 was marked as Ext. 1. The petition filed by the defendant to the chairman of the Union Parishad on 19.3.72 was marked as Ext. 2 and the Ext. 3 is the order passed in the salish. The suit was decreed by the Trial Court and on being aggrieved the defendant went to appeal. The Appellate Court dismissed the appeal on contest and thus the judgment of the decree of the Trial Court was affirmed. Being aggrieved by the judgment of the Court of appeal below the defendant moved this revisional application before this Court and obtained the instant Rule. 

 5. Mr. Hasan Foez Siddique, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-petitioner, submits' that the learned Courts below erred in law on the fact of the record in decreeing the suit for Specific Performance of Contract without any valid ground and cogent reason and thus decisions of the Courts below have occasioned a failure of justice. 

 6. The learned Advocate then submits that the plaintiffs case as made out on the basis of alleged oral agreement between the parties for reconveyance of the suit land has ultimately been given a go by and instead introduced the story of settlement arrived at in the salish held by chairman of the local Union Parishad consequent on the application filed by the defendant for restoration of possession of the suit land from which he was dispossessed during the liberation war period in 1971 and, therefore, the Court of appeal below committed error of law in decreeing the suit on the face of such contradictory claims. The learned advocate further submits that the learned Court of appeal below erred in law in his decision occasioning failure of justice in not holding that according to the provision of sections 91 and 92 of the Evidence Act oral evidence is inadmissible to alter or contradict the contents of a registered instrument. 

 9. The learned Trial Court found Ext. 1 is out and out the sale deed and the defendant got the land by the sale deed executed and registered on 2.10.63 absolutely free from all encumbrances. The Trial Court also found that the Ext, 3 which is the judgment of the conciliation Court given in a salish was made during the pendency of the suit and as such no cause of action for the suit thereby arose and hence he had kept Ext. 3 out of consideration in the suit. The learned Trial Court, however, took into consideration factum of possession of the suit land by the plaintiffs as the foundation of the claim of the plaintiffs for getting the land reconveyed in their favour. Thus the finding of the learned Trial Court is not based on legal evidence but on inference only. The Court of appeal below found that the plaintiffs are bound by the terms of the kabala but he went further in holding that the defendant cannot go back from his own conduct as he agreed to reconvey the land to the plaintiffs on payment of Tk. 1000.00. In arriving at such a finding the learned Appellate Court took into consideration the Ext. 2, the application filed by the defendant before the chairman of the Local Union Parishad for getting back the possession of the suit land from which he was dispossessed by the plaintiff during the liberation war period and Ext. 3 the decision arrived at by the chairman in the salish, the fact which was kept out of consideration by the Trial Court. The Trial Court decreed the suit for the reconveyance of the suit land on payment of consideration money of Tk. 4000.00 as mentioned in the sale deed Ext. 1 with the finding that the transfer was with agreement for reconveyance. The Appellate Court below affirmed the finding of the Trial Court without applying his independent judicial mind. Finding of the both the courts are erroneous in view of the fact the registered sale deed Ext. 1 neither does contain any agreement for reconveyance, nor there exist any contemporaneous written instrument embodying such terms. The plaintiff has miserably failed to prove the existence of any agreement made between the parties for the reconveyance. 

 11. Both the Courts below found that the land was transferred to the defendant by registered instrument Ext. 1 and that it is out and out a sale deed. Therefore on the face of such registered instrument and in the absence of any contemporaneous written instrument I do not consider the oral evidence to be at all sufficient to hold that there was any agreement between the plaintiffs and the defendants for getting a decree for reconveyance of the suit land: Relying on the established rule of evidence that the oral evidence is inadmissible for the purpose of asserting the intention of the parties on the face of registered instrument, I hold that the defendant got the land vide registered sale deed Ext. 1 which is not subjected to any agreement for reconveyance of the land. For the reasons stated above I am of the view that decision of the courts below decreeing the suit is erroneous being against the principle of law laid down under sections 91 and 92 of the Evidence Act and judicial pronouncements made in this respect. 

 12. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence of the Court below I hold that the judgments and decrees of the Courts below cannot be sustained and hence those are set aside resulting in the dismissal of the suit.
